beats.comprehensionObjective: Recognize a timekeeper can assist an east–west navigation problem.
beats.continuityRequirements: Reference and ship identities persist; every later angle is measured from the same reference.
beats.disclosureRequirements: Conceptual scene, not historical voyage footage; longitude is angular east–west position.
beats.mustCommunicate: A ship and ordinary TIME indication supply the information gap; establish a known reference meridian and an unresolved ship meridian.
beats.mustNotImply: No complete position fix, longitude pointer on the clock, latitude value or GPS behavior.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Understand the timekeeper carries time tied to somewhere known.
beats.continuityRequirements: Same reference origin and carried timekeeper persist through comparison and payoff.
beats.disclosureRequirements: Reference time is mean solar time; displayed value is corrected for known clock error, with date/day ambiguity resolved.
beats.mustCommunicate: Separate the reference location from the ship; carried reference reading stays tied to that location rather than being reset to local time.
beats.mustNotImply: Not a clock remotely receiving an eighteenth-century live signal; not universal historical Greenwich.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Understand observation supplies local time and the solar observation must be corrected to a comparable basis.
beats.continuityRequirements: Distinguish the carried reference reading from the local observation throughout; local readout is a derived display, not a second independent historical marine clock.
beats.disclosureRequirements: Corrected to match means converting apparent solar time to mean solar time with the equation of time, not a time-zone change or resetting the ship clock. No date-specific correction number or new noon geometry is asserted.
beats.mustCommunicate: Sun-derived APPARENT SOLAR TIME is converted to LOCAL MEAN SOLAR TIME before the example. Required factual disclosure: BOTH MEAN SOLAR TIME.
beats.mustNotImply: Do not compare raw sundial/noon observation with uncorrected mean-clock time. Do not make a sundial or second carried clock magically give local time.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Understand this is a simultaneous spatial comparison rather than a ship journey lasting two hours.
beats.continuityRequirements: Shared instant is retained in the numerical example; neither reading advances alone.
beats.disclosureRequirements: Illustrative comparison, not claimed measured voyage data.
beats.mustCommunicate: Lock both corrected readings to ONE INSTANT; required disclosure SAME INSTANT.
beats.mustNotImply: No elapsed-voyage inference from the difference; no comparison of different dates without resolving day branch.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Understand why different meridians have different local solar times and why the time gap maps to an angle.
beats.continuityRequirements: Keep viewing orientation and east direction unambiguous;15° marks longitude angle, not latitude or orbital angle.
beats.disclosureRequirements: SCHEMATIC / SOLAR-TIME RELATIONSHIP. Geometry may express reviewed angles; the physical scene is not a precision astronomical simulation.
beats.mustCommunicate: Relate Sun/Earth meridians to a labeled15° angle per1h of consistent solar-time difference.
beats.mustNotImply: No exact360° stellar-relative rotation in24SIhours; no civil-zone boundaries or universal distance per degree.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Understand12:00 reference and14:00 local are simultaneous comparable readings.
beats.continuityRequirements: Maintain same reference origin, same instant and corrected-time basis from earlier beats.
beats.disclosureRequirements: These are illustrative mean times; no actual date, historical voyage or measured clock error is introduced.
beats.mustCommunicate: Show12:00 reference and14:00 local with BOTH MEAN SOLAR TIME / SAME INSTANT / ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE; identify two in the afternoon as14:00.
beats.mustNotImply: Do not call12:00 apparent local noon or mark14:00 as noon; no unrestricted ordinary wall-clock time-zone comparison.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Understand local time ahead corresponds to east, and2×15° gives30°.
beats.continuityRequirements: Same ship/reference meridians; eastward angular displacement is consistent with the earlier view and time relation.
beats.disclosureRequirements: Illustrative calculation, not a claim of perfect navigation or exact historical position.
beats.mustCommunicate: Convert +2h local-minus-reference into +30° EAST OF THE REFERENCE; required factual label30°E RELATIVE TO REFERENCE.
beats.mustNotImply: Never reverse east/west, draw30° latitude, present complete geographic position or equate30° with a universal distance.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Recognize Harrison’s important contribution without replacing the mechanism with biography.
beats.continuityRequirements: Historical device identity remains distinct from generic illustrative time readouts; do not imply the12:00/14:00 example is H4’s recorded trial.
beats.disclosureRequirements: H4 object identity is an editorial factual requirement, not a choice of medium. Any future reconstruction or collection photograph requires accuracy/rights review; no media selected.
beats.mustCommunicate: Identify H4 as a large LONGITUDE WATCH; associate it with John Harrison and qualified sea-going timekeeping demonstration.
beats.mustNotImply: No sole invention of longitude, first-ever universal timekeeper, instant fleet adoption, full-prize claim, later boxed chronometer substituted forH4, or detailed unsupported mechanism.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Understand marine clocks did not erase other longitude approaches.
beats.continuityRequirements: This complements the local solar observation already needed; other astronomical methods are distinct from that local-time observation.
beats.disclosureRequirements: A generic indication of astronomy is sufficient; detailed lunar geometry, tables or figures would add claims and require upstream review.
beats.mustCommunicate: Preserve a complementary astronomical-method indication alongside the timekeeper concept.
beats.mustNotImply: Do not show astronomy disappearing, lunar distances mandatory for every clock-based fix, or all ships instantly replacing dead reckoning.

beats.comprehensionObjective: Leave the viewer with the correct causal system.
beats.continuityRequirements: Return to the existing comparison and angular result; do not introduce another location, instrument or factual relationship.
beats.disclosureRequirements: Preserve relative reference, corrected mean-time basis, simultaneous readings and illustrative status in any final factual presentation.
beats.mustCommunicate: Resolve REFERENCE TIME + LOCAL OBSERVATION/TIME + COMPARISON/CALCULATION → LONGITUDE, using the same corrected example and reference.
beats.mustNotImply: Clock time is not a position display; longitude alone does not establish latitude or complete position; not a navigation tutorial guaranteeing accuracy.
